title: Graded compatibility for structured schemas, partial-emits reconciliation, and idempotent function-bridge acceptance
creator: Ravi Menon
description: Scope: Define acceptance criteria and testable requirements for a graded schema compatibility model, deterministic partial-emits reconciliation during streaming responses, and explicit idempotent bridging semantics for function/tool invocations. This ticket captures PM-level requirements, trade-offs considered with engineering, observable signals to be emitted for telemetry, and a minimal manual and automated test matrix. The goal is to reduce production breakage during schema evolution while preserving low-latency streaming and safe tool handoffs. Out of scope: full runtime kernel selection changes and model-side generation logic (handled in ENG sub-issues).
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility levels defined and implemented: LEVEL_STRICT (no unknown fields allowed), LEVEL_TOLERANT (unknown fields tolerated but logged), LEVEL_PROGRESSIVE (best-effort merging with deprecation metadata). Each level must be selectable per API route and documented in the API spec.

Schema negotiation handshake: on session start the server must return a schema-version header (X-RW-Schema-Version) and a compatibility-level echo. If client sends explicit schema_version in start frame, server must accept or return 409 with suggested migration hints.

Streaming partial-emits reconciliation: streaming responses must include checkpoint tokens (field: rw_checkpoint_id) at deterministic boundaries. If a stream disconnects, client can resume by sending last seen rw_checkpoint_id; server must deterministically deduplicate and resume from next token without re-invoking external tools unless required by non-idempotent state transition rules (see idempotency rules below).

Idempotent function-bridge semantics: function/tool invocations initiated by the model must include a uuid (rw_invoke_id) and an invocation intent header describing side-effects. For invocations marked 'idempotent', retries after network failures must not cause duplicate effects; for 'non-idempotent' invocations, the platform must document explicit retry boundaries and surface a deterministic failure code to the client for operator-driven remediation.

Error modes and fallback behaviors: define and implement these runtime-visible error classes: SCHEMA_MISMATCH, PARTIAL_EMIT_LOSS, INVOKE_RATE_LIMIT, INVOKE_NON_IDEMPOTENT_REJECT, BACKPRESSURE_THROTTLE. Each error must map to a stable error code, human-readable message, and recommended client action in the API docs.

Observability: server must emit metrics and traces for schema_mismatch_rate, partial_emit_resume_success, avg_resume_latency, rw_checkpoint_gap, and invoke_idempotency_conflicts. Sample payload diffs (max 100 samples/hour per route) should be stored in the structured-output debug stream for investigation dashboards.

Automated e2e tests: regression suite must include tests for resuming a stream from checkpoint under simulated packet loss and for replaying an idempotent invocation without duplicate side-effects (mocks accepted). Tests must pass on CI across 3 model variants in the catalog (small/medium/large) before rollout.

Fallback policy acceptance: when compatibility level is LEVEL_TOLERANT or LEVEL_PROGRESSIVE and a strict-only field is encountered, the system must either (a) drop unknown fields and emit SCHEMA_MISMATCH telemetry, or (b) surface a structured warning object in-stream (rw_warning) and continue. The default policy must be documented and configurable by customers on dedicated/private tiers.

Contract tests for clients: publish a lightweight client conformance suite (JS + Python) that validates resume semantics, checkpoint tokens, and idempotent invocation replay. The client suite must be runnable locally and in CI.

Migration guidance: produce a two-page migration checklist for customers that includes how to opt-into LEVEL_TOLERANT, how to read schema diff telemetry, and recommended rollouts for model version bumps that change schema (canary -> 25% -> 100%).
notes: Trade-offs: strict compatibility is safest for enterprise fintech/legal customers but increases breakage during rapid product iteration. The graded approach allows product teams to default to tolerant modes in experimentation while enterprises lock down strict mode.

Decision: wire telemetry now; operator controls for default compatibility level will be an admin setting in Dedicated/Private. Hosted default should be LEVEL_PROGRESSIVE for non-SLA accounts and LEVEL_STRICT for enterprise tenants unless overridden.
Engineering ask: need an infra ticket to reserve storage for structured-output debug stream (per-tenant retention). See ENG-20012 in dependencies.
Conformance: security review required because debug payloads may contain PII if customers don't redact; plan for KMS encryption of debug stream in Private installs.
